I'm not against Uber and I'm certainly not in favour of the ridiculous fares for cabbies in Toronto but I can understand why they are mad. The city just needs to find a way for them to co-exist. The answer is to let the markets decide. If the taxi industry is outdated and bloated because of regulations, licensing, fees, bureaucracy etc, then let it whither and die on the vine. Taxi Drivers are about as qualified as I am (I would wager I'm a better driver than a lot of taxi drivers around) and Ottawa's Blue Cab has a notorious reputation for sexual assault charges, property theft and dangerous driving. The licenses cab drivers get are dependent on their ability to pay for them and afford an insurance rider.

Electricians, on the other hand, train for 4-6 years and attend college and write tests to receive their licenses. Different bowl of soup and the system works fine.

I've lived in many different countries, some of which had deregulated free-market transit options and for the most part they work fine. Prices are affordable and I never had problems.

We, however, have a big problem here with legalized corruption and monopolies enforced with state power. Fuck that. Bring on Uber.
